55.text: CAP theorem states that a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance. Since network partitions are unavoidable, systems must choose between CP (consistent but may be unavailable during partitions) or AP (available but may return stale data).
key_points: Consistency: all nodes see same data simultaneously
Availability: every request receives a response
Partition tolerance: system works despite network splits
Real systems: CP (HBase, Zookeeper) vs AP (Cassandra, DynamoDB)

56.text: ACID properties ensure reliable database transactions. Atomicity means transactions are all-or-nothing. Consistency ensures the database moves from one valid state to another. Isolation means concurrent transactions do not interfere. Durability guarantees committed data survives failures.
key_points: Atomicity: all operations succeed or all fail

57.text: The transformer uses self-attention mechanisms instead of recurrence. Multi-head attention allows the model to attend to different positions simultaneously. Positional encoding preserves sequence order. The encoder processes input and the decoder generates output, with cross-attention connecting them.
key_points: Self-attention: each token attends to all others

58.text: Bias measures error from incorrect assumptions in the model. Variance measures sensitivity to training data fluctuations. High bias causes underfitting, high variance causes overfitting. Total error equals bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Regularization reduces variance at the cost of slight bias increase.
key_points: Bias: systematic error from wrong assumptions
Variance: error from sensitivity to training data

59.text: React's reconciliation algorithm determines the minimum set of DOM operations needed when state changes. It builds a virtual DOM tree, diffs it with the previous tree, and applies only the necessary updates. Keys help React identify which list items changed, improving diff performance.
key_points: Component type changes cause full remount

60.text: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when nodes are added or removed. A hash ring maps both nodes and keys to positions. Each key is served by the first node clockwise on the ring. Virtual nodes improve load distribution.
key_points: Hash ring with nodes and keys
Only K/N keys remapped when node added
Used in distributed caches and databases

61.text: Batch gradient descent uses all samples per update (stable but slow). Stochastic uses one sample (fast but noisy). Mini-batch balances both. Adam optimizer combines momentum and adaptive learning rates, making it the default choice for most deep learning tasks.
key_points: SGD: noisy but fast, good generalization

62.text: JSON Web Tokens contain three Base64-encoded parts: header (algorithm), payload (claims), and signature. The server signs tokens with a secret key. Clients store tokens and send them in the Authorization header. Stateless: the server verifies the signature without database lookup.
key_points: Signature: HMAC-SHA256 of header and payload

63.text: Random forest builds multiple decision trees on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets. Predictions are aggregated by majority vote (classification) or averaging (regression). The randomness decorrelates trees, reducing variance significantly compared to a single tree.
key_points: Bagging: bootstrap sampling of training data
Random feature subset at each split
OOB error as free validation estimate

64.text: HTTP is request-response: client always initiates. WebSocket provides full-duplex communication over a persistent connection. After HTTP upgrade handshake, both sides can send messages freely. WebSocket is ideal for real-time features like chat, live updates, and collaborative tools.
key_points: Lower latency than polling for real-time
